transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-11
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Tara Singh (MediCore Head of ML), Carlos Vega (Infra Lead), Marta Lopez (Security)

Summary: quick check-in on onboarding progress, validating infra access, and next steps for benchmark run.

[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, quick roll call — Alex here, Priya's with me from the SE team.
[00:08] Tara (MediCore): Hi, Tara here. We have Carlos and Marta as well.
[00:12] Carlos (MediCore): Yep, hi all.
[00:14] Marta (MediCore): Morning.
[00:18] Alex: Cool. The goal for today is to make sure you have the service account + network access we need, confirm the env readiness, and lock a slot for the perf run next week. Priya, do you want to start with the env checklist?
[00:28] Priya (Redwood SE): Sure. I put the checklist in the pilot doc we shared, but quick highlights: we need a scoped service account or API key for the Redwood hosted pilot; if you want private deployment we'll need VPC peering and a bastion. For hosted, just IP allowlist and service key is enough. Carlos, what's your preferred approach?
[00:47] Carlos: For now we prefer hosted with VPC peering later. We're constrained on infra ops bandwidth so hosted simplifies things. We'll do IP allowlist and a service account.
[00:57] Alex: Great. For the service account scope, we only need outbound https to api.redwood.ai and S3 access for model artifacts if you plan to use private model storage. But you can also point to Redwood-managed model registry — which requires less config.
[01:13] Tara: We want to try your recommended open-model first, and then test our custom weights. So S3 access will be needed. Carlos, can you provision a bucket and an IAM role?
[01:23] Carlos: Yeah, I'll create a bucket and a role and share the ARN. Quick Q: do you need KMS access too?
[01:28] Priya: If you're encrypting at rest and you want us to fetch artifacts, we need decrypt permission for a customer-managed KMS key, or you can upload to a Redwood presigned path. Either works.
[01:38] Marta: From security side, we need to review SOC2 and encryption detail. Alex, can you send over the SOC2 and a network diagram?
[01:45] Alex: Yes, I'll send SOC2 + our security pack after the call.
[01:49] Marta: Also, we need audit logs retained for 12 months and RBAC controls — do you support per-team roles?
[01:55] Priya: We do support RBAC and audit logs. For the hosted API we can enable token-level logging and export to your SIEM via webhook or S3. Retention options are configurable.
[02:05] Tara: Nice. On the perf side, our target is p95 latency under 400ms on inference for 2k token average, and cost within X — we still need a baseline.
[02:15] Priya: Ok we'll run a 10k token benchmark with your representative prompt set. Note: costs scale with tokens; we'll provide an estimated unit cost after the run. Also we'll test both quantized and float configs to show tradeoffs.
[02:28] Carlos: For the benchmark, can you run it from a Redwood-hosted runner so we don't need to spin up machines here?
[02:33] Priya: Yes we can run it from Redwood Dedicated capacity or hosted infra. For the pilot we'll use hosted unless you want dedicated reserved GPUs. Hosted will emulate production but dedicated gives more stable latency.
[02:45] Alex: To be explicit: Hosted pilot = fast to start, variable latency at scale. Dedicated = predictable throughput, but requires reserved capacity. For POC we usually start hosted to prove quality then move to dedicated for SLA-sensitive workloads.
[02:59] Tara: That makes sense. We'll start hosted.
[03:02] Marta: A couple of security clarifications — data residency: our data must stay in EU. Is there a region option?
[03:09] Alex: Yes, we have EU regions; we'll ensure the pilot runs in eu-west. I'll note that in the action items.
[03:16] Tara: Great. Also, SSO: we need SAML for console access.
[03:20] Alex: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. We'll send the SSO setup guide.
[03:25] Carlos: Network rules — for IP allowlist, what's the egress IP range?
[03:29] Priya: We'll send the IP ranges; for the pilot we'll give a short list of CIDRs. For VPC peering later, we can coordinate peering and route tables.
[03:38] Tara: Sounds good.
[03:40] Alex: Ok, let's walk through current blockers: are there any open access issues?
[03:44] Carlos: I haven't created the role yet, but I will after this call. The only blocker is KMS permission confirmation.
[03:49] Marta: And I'm compiling compliance questions — nothing blocking for pilot.
[03:53] Priya: For the perf test we need the prompt set and expected seq lengths — Tara, can you share a small sample of 50 prompts and an average token count?
[04:02] Tara: Yes — I'll share a sample set and the expected PII redaction tags.
[04:06] Priya: Perfect. We'll also enable KV cache emulation in the workload to more closely match expected patterns. Note: sometimes transcripts come back with K V cache spelled out, but we mean key-value cache.
[04:20] Carlos: One nit — you mentioned Redwood Dedicated earlier, but sometimes transcript or doc says 'red wood dedicate'— just clarifying.
[04:26] Alex: Haha yeah, transcription artifacts. It's Redwood Dedicated.
[04:29] Marta: On logging, does the hosted pilot expose per-token cost immediately?
[04:33] Alex: We can show token-level cost estimates in the console; exact billing reconciliation happens post-pilot.
[04:39] Tara: Ok, timeline — can we do the benchmark the week of March 16th?
[04:44] Priya: Yes, we have availability on Tue/Wed. Prefer Tue 2026-03-17 morning UTC.
[04:50] Carlos: Tue works for us.
[04:52] Alex: I'll pencil 2026-03-17 09:00 UTC and send a calendar invite for the live run.
[04:58] Priya: For the run I'll need the service account key and S3 access by COB 2026-03-13 so I can set up the runner.
[05:06] Alex: Noted.
[05:08] Marta: I'll send the compliance question list by 2026-03-14.
[05:12] Tara: Any outstanding items?
[05:14] Carlos: Nothing on infra besides provisioning the role.
[05:16] Priya: I will also prepare a short perf plan doc so you know the metrics we'll capture (p50/p95/p99, throughput, cost per 1k tokens).
[05:25] Alex: Great. Quick recap of next steps and owners: Alex sends SOC2 + security pack + IP ranges; Carlos shares service account and S3 role; Priya prepares benchmark script and schedule; Marta shares compliance questions; Tara shares prompt sample. We'll follow up in Slack and update the pilot doc.
[05:43] Tara: Thanks everyone.
[05:45] Alex: Thanks all, talk soon.

End of transcript.

References/Links: Pilot doc (shared Google Drive link), Security pack (link to SSO + SOC2 in email), Benchmark spreadsheet (link)
